content.title: Freezing rain/drizzle possible overnight before even warmer weather arrives
content.text: There is a lot of moisture in our snow pack from this week's system, and we added about another inch last night, too. Snow depth in Eau Claire is about 10" but of course is tough to measure as there are a lot of drifts. With much warmer air on the way, expect a lot of melting through the rest of the week. If your curbs look like this, standing water could become a problem in your neighborhood and around your house. With overnight lows below freezing, that standing water can create very slippery ice at the ends of driveways and in roads. Consider adopting a storm drain near your house and shoveling a path to it so water has a place to drain. If you live in a rural area, consider shoveling a path for water to get down into ditches. Doing so is beneficial to you and your neighbors, and city/county crews could not possibly get to all of them if that were their job (which it isn't). Some light rain or drizzle is possible within a round of scattered showers overnight. With temps dropping to near or below freezing, that could become freezing rain/drizzle. That would create a layer of ice on roads that would cause slippery stretches to ice covered roads. That would create some slippery spots or even ice-covered roads if precip falls when temps are at/below freezing. The best chance for rain or drizzle is in the middle of the night and the best chance for subfreezing temps are within a few hours on either side of sunrise.Again, if any rain or drizzle lingers when temps are below freezing, roads will become very slippery. Temps will get even warmer each day through Saturday when temps could be in the 60s.A system will move through Saturday night with a slight chance for rain or wintry mix through the first half of Sunday. After which, temps will be a bit cooler but still near average to start the week with slow warming early next week.
